_comment: Policy of tools/sim/sim_audit.py. excluded: the REVIEWED list of translation units that are not simulation code (glob relative to engine/, or <build>/... for generated and staged sources, with the reason); every other source must be in OPENBFME_SIM_SOURCES. facade_files / facade_functions: the registered facade implementations where floating arithmetic and math calls are the implementation (pinned by tools/sim/test_sim_audit.py).

excluded.reason: lane HUD-5: the drawable decorations (health bars, construction text, veterancy marks) as 2D draw operations: user interface, reads the logic and the drawables, never changes them

lane HUD-5: the players screen's Status rows (names, faction texts, team and status labels, colours for the movie): user interface, built from a resolved GameInfo and const queries of the live players, never read by the logic
the loading screen's cards (names, faction texts, colours for the movie): user interface, built from a resolved GameInfo, never read by the logic
wall-clock diagnostics of the device layer (load and frame timings in reports): never simulation state

generated sources: the byte tables of the embedded data files (EmbeddedData.gen.cpp, cmake/EmbedFiles.cmake) and the build's version strings (BuildVersion.gen.cpp, cmake/BuildVersion.cmake, lane RELEASE-1): no arithmetic

the staged Lua 4.0.1 library with EA's fork (C sources + leanumeric.cpp): its number arithmetic is the PC24 emulation of the retail VM by design (LUA-1, tools/lua_patch_check.py, tests/test_lua_runtime.cpp); not scanned by the AST check (stop S-230)
the EA Apt menu / UI player: client-side user interface, never part of the simulation state

lane FX-2: the live game's client effect player (FXList / particle playback of the logic's effect events, EnteringStateFX, ParticleSysBone systems, effect sounds): reads the logic and the drawables, draws only the CLIENT random stream, never writes simulation state

lane FX-3: the draw scripts' view of the object's target (CurDrawableIsCurrentTargetKindof / CurDrawableGetCurrentTargetBearing, RW 0x73667D / 0x734A75): copies the logic's target record, answers only draw scripts, never writes simulation state

lane RENDER-2: the construction look of a drawable (the build-up animation frame and the height offset of a structure being built, RW 0x4B51B5 / 0x4B686D): reads the object, writes only draw frames and render offsets, never simulation state

lane CAMP-1: the GDExtension's campaign list, a campaign mission's load options (LiveGame::Options), the mission's end as the script engine reports it and the progress sidecar file; it reads logic state between frames and never writes it

lane CAH-1: the profile's and the archives' Create-a-Hero files (list, save, delete, the unique id from the client's random device): menu data; a hero reaches the logic only through the game setup's record
lane CAH-1: the hero the Create-a-Hero builder screen edits (slots, points, providers): user interface, never simulation state
lane CAH-1: the Create-a-Hero builder screen (CreateAHero.apt and its pages): user interface, never simulation state
lane CAH-2: the user data folder from the install's gi.dat (the Create-a-Hero save folder): files, never simulation state
lane CAH-2: the ColorPicker render component of the menus (externs, texel pick): user interface, never simulation state

lane SCRIPT-1: GameWorld's view of the map script engine (the client requests handed to the script camera director, the engine's report, a waypoint lookup): reads the logic, never writes simulation state

lane SCRIPT-3: HAS_FINISHED_AUDIO's audio length model (stop S-1187): reads the audio INI and the archives' audio headers and returns whole milliseconds by integer arithmetic (frames * 1000 / rate) to the logic's timer list; the audio headers' float helpers it includes are not called
lane CAMP-1H: TheVideoPlayer's Video INI blocks, the movie file lookup and its VP6 header (the client's movie presentation and its audio events); no logic state
lane CAMP-2: the movies' VP6 picture decoder and EA's movie container (client presentation on the render clock); no logic state
lane CAMP-1: TheLinearCampaignManager's LinearCampaign INI blocks and the shell's campaign progress (which mission to load next); no logic state, the logic gets only the map name and the difficulty
lane SCRIPT-1: the client half of the script engine's camera / letterbox / caption / fade requests on the render clock; the logic only records the requests and never reads this state

lane END-1: the client half of the end of a game (the local player's end screen, messages and Eva, the human player's win / loss script library run over the logic snapshot, the score screen data copied when the game is left): reads the logic, never writes simulation state

lane STEALTH-1: the stealth look of a drawable for the local player (hidden for an enemy, the friend's opacity pulse in client time, RW 0x6760F9): reads the logic snapshot, writes only draw opacity, never simulation state
Apt canvas: UI drawing
UI font substitution
localised UI text (the game's .str files)

the W3D rendering and asset library (meshes, hierarchies, animations, shaders, textures): client-side drawing; animation poses are cosmetic here (the logic reads bone positions only through the draw-module contracts of the later lanes, which will be classified then)
the W3D device layer: draw modules, terrain meshes, height map UVs, asset catalog: client-side rendering
draw module setup of map objects: client side
terrain texture atlas: rendering
road geometry: rendering
water mesh: rendering
TGA image reader: textures
weather particle parameters: rendering
map list cache (MapCache.ini equivalent): file I/O and listing
BIG archive file system on Win32 handles: file I/O
refpack / compression codecs: byte stream decoding
text file and path helpers: file I/O
archive file abstraction: file I/O
archive file system: file I/O
loose file scan: file I/O
which retail archives load (policy JSON): file I/O
MD5 of files: integrity checking
JSON reader of the embedded archive policies: tooling data
string utility: no numeric simulation values
host pacing: decides how many logic frames run per wall-clock interval, never what a frame computes (the state hash is frame indexed)
FX-1 client-side effects (FXList playback, particle systems, emitters): visual only, driven by the CLIENT random generator (GameClientRandom), never read back by the logic

the client (visual) random variables of the FX / particle code: a separate generator from the logic RNG (RandomValue.cpp), not part of the state hash

APT-4 GUI shell: windows, gadgets and Apt screens, client-side user interface; the only values it hands to the logic are the skirmish GameInfo, built by the (simulation-classified) src/GameClient/GUI/Skirmish sources

lane CAMP-2: VP6MovieStream, a movie's frames decoded into a texture on the render clock (client presentation); no logic state
GDExtension class registration: engine glue, no game values
reads the retail archives through Godot file access: file I/O
builds Godot meshes from W3D models: rendering
builds Godot materials / shaders from W3D shader state: rendering
instances and poses W3D models on the GPU: rendering (reads logic transforms, writes none)
binds the host frame clock to the LogicFrameClock: host pacing (decides how many frames run, not what they compute)
builds the terrain meshes and textures from the map: rendering (reads TerrainLogic, writes none)
builds the Godot scene nodes of the map's objects for display: rendering (reads the retail object world, creates no logic objects)
hosts the Apt menu player: user interface
lane HUD-4: decodes the install's packed textures (.dds / .jpg + .png) for the Apt player and the HUD: drawing
a debug view that draws the pathfinder grid and a path of its own pathfinder instance: it writes no state of a running game
converts the 3D colour buffer around the transparent pass (gamma-space compositing, RENDER-3 / S-831): rendering only
the map's colour grade on the 3D colour buffer (LookupTablePostEffect, RENDER-4 / S-1650): rendering only
plays FXLists and particle systems on the GPU: client-side effects (FX-1)

AUDIO-1, client audio: decoders, the audio INI blocks, the AudioManager and the simulated device; the logic only posts fire-and-forget requests through AudioApi and reads nothing back, so no audio state or arithmetic reaches the lockstep state
AUDIO-1, the Eva announcer: client-side speech selection and cooldowns, driven by events the logic reports; it writes no logic state
AUDIO-1, the Godot audio device (voices, buses, streams): client output only

AUDIO-2, the in-game music (the music map's scripts run on the client): reads the logic, keeps its own flags / counters / timers, drives the audio manager's music; writes no logic state, draws only from the audio random stream

AUDIO-4, the footsteps (AnimationSoundClientBehavior and TheAnimationSoundModuleManager): a ClientBehavior module of the drawables; reads the drawables' animation frames and the listener, plays on the audio manager; never read by the logic
AUDIO-2, the audio side of a live game: the owner resolver and player queries of the audio manager and the object ambient sounds; reads the logic, writes no logic state

AUDIO-2, the unit voice picker: client presentation (reads the selection and the logic, plays through AudioApi / Eva); its recently-said memory is client state keyed by object id, it writes no logic state
the tactical view's projection and ray maths (client camera state: a click's ground point is chosen by the clicking peer and travels as message data)
client-side picking (ray against object volumes) and selection predicates: input interpretation, never read by the logic
QA-1, the HUD's pick ray against the drawn W3D models (client input interpretation: the picked id travels as message data; a client cache of model triangles)
mouse.ini drag tolerances: client input settings

lane INPUT-1, the HotKeyTranslator (RW 0x75B068): a released key presses the command button its label marks; client input interpretation, the press goes through ControlBar::pressButton whose messages ControlBarCommandProcessing.cpp builds (manifested)
the CommandMap and the key / mouse button translator: client input interpretation, no simulation arithmetic
the in-game HUD component: client user interface
the Palantir screen: client user interface
the Godot HUD node: camera, input events and drawing of the device layer
the control bar view model (button states, queue display, money): client user interface reading the logic; the messages a press builds are in ControlBarCommandProcessing.cpp (manifested)
the radar picture: client user interface reading the logic
the mouse cursor file decoder (RIFF / ICO bytes): client user interface
the GameData camera fields and the map's camera values: client camera input settings (CAM-1)
the retail tactical camera (W3DView): client camera state, never read by the logic and not in the state hash; its float maths is not compared between peers (CAM-1)
the LookAt translator: raw input to camera movement, client state; it emits no GameMessage (CAM-1)

lane PROJ-2: the drawable's fade (RW 0x85EE00 / 0x67309D / 0x675AB7: a launched projectile hidden for InvisibleFrames, then faded in; the fog fades): reads a completed frame's snapshot and template data, writes only the drawable's opacity and hidden flag, never simulation state

lane SMOOTH-1: the drawable's render pose between two logic frames (lerp / slerp of the recorded and current object transform by the clock's alpha): reads the object, writes only the drawable's render transform, never simulation state

lane SMOOTH-1 (S-810): the recorder of the simulation's client calls (drawable creation / destruction, model conditions, module and sub object visibility, placement) as ordered data-only events; it reads the object and writes only its event list. Its one answer to the simulation (showModule) is a template tag lookup, no arithmetic
lane SMOOTH-1 (S-810): the immutable render snapshot of a completed logic frame (copies of transforms, positions, construction state); reads the logic between frames, writes only the snapshot

lane SMOOTH-1 (S-810): LiveGame's render-side presentation (presented frame and alpha, client events applied in order, poses from one snapshot) and the logic worker's thread management; the frames themselves run in LiveGame::runFrameOwned (LiveGame.cpp, audited)

lane MP-1: the UDP socket and the reliable per-peer delivery (resends, acks, the test harness's loss and delay): it decides WHEN a peer's bytes arrive, never what a logic frame contains (GameNetwork/Network.h decides that from the received data alone)
lane UI-2: the Godot viewer of an Apt View3D render object (a W3D model in a sub viewport composited into the menu); client presentation only
lane UI-2: the player's Options.ini (ZH UserPreferences as RotWK's OptionPreferences); client settings only, never read by the simulation
lane UI-2: the animation clock of an Apt View3D render object (the end screen's rings, the shell's menu frame); client presentation only
lane UI-1: RotWK's message box (GuiFX.apt's MessageBox clip: its texts, Show / Hide, the button commands); client presentation only

lane MP-2: DisconnectScreen.apt's engine side (texts, the movie's bar and kick-button functions, the Kick / Quit buttons handed to the host); the disconnect path itself (GameNetwork/DisconnectManager.cpp) is audited
lane MP-2: the desync dump file (RW 0x6290C7's DESYNC-*.txt): it writes the exchanged hash breakdowns and copies the replay; it reads no logic state
lane MP-2: SaveLoad.apt's replay page (the list the host gives, the chosen file handed back as a shell request); no logic state

lane MP-2: the LAN lobby (finding games, joining, the setup's options, chat, the start): sockets and time; what it produces is the NewGameMessage every peer starts from (encoded by NetPacket.cpp, audited)
lane MP-2: LanLobby.apt's engine side (the game list, the setup gadgets on the LAN lobby's model); no logic state
lane MP-1: the host / join lobby datagrams before the game: it hands every peer the same NewGameMessage (the logic's input, encoded by NetPacket.cpp which is audited); no logic state

lane MP-1: the headless peer process (argument parsing, the wall-clock loop, the report files) and its scripted test player, an input source like the HUD: its commands enter the logic only through the lockstep command list
lane MP-1: the scripted test player (headless peer --script, the two-window demo): an input source like the HUD; its commands enter the logic only through the lockstep command list

lane MP-1: the immutable profile identity (build id, owned format versions, numeric mode, RNG, mounted archives' md5 in mount order) peers and replays compare before a game starts; never part of the logic state
the Palantir's portrait choice (HUD-2): reads the selection and the templates' image names for the movie, never writes simulation state
the spell book screens' engine side (lane SPELL-2): display reads of the logic and GameMessages it builds; never simulation state
lane RELEASE-1: finding and checking the player's game folders before anything is mounted (registry, Wine prefixes, the archive list); launcher code, never simulation state
lane RELEASE-1: removes the home folder and the user name from log lines; text only, never simulation state
lane RELEASE-1: routes stdout / stderr through the log privacy filter; console text only, never simulation state
lane RELEASE-1: the version line of the logs and the main menu; text only
lane RELEASE-1: the Godot view of the install finder, the version and the session log file; client only, never simulation state
